title: Effectiveness of the concept of prehabilitation before gastric and esophageal surgery
summary:
Preoperative rehabilitation, also known as prehabilitation, is a means of enhancing postoperative recovery. It includes multimodal programs with physical, nutritional and/or psychological interventions aimed at optimizing the physical and psychological condition of patients before esophagectomy and reducing postoperative complications, accelerating recovery and increasing general resilience preoperatively. A period of four to six weeks pre-hospitalization is often used for prehabilitation, especially if neoadjuvant treatment has been given beforehand (in parallel). Although there is growing evidence that prehabilitation improves postoperative outcomes after abdominal surgery in general, there is limited evidence specifically for esophagectomy. However, since patients with esophageal cancer often already have health impairments prior to surgery (malnutrition, including cachexia, advanced age) and are at higher risk for postoperative complications, they could particularly benefit from prehabilitation.
Our study aims to investigate the concept of prehabilitation consisting of an exercise program, supportive nutritional therapy, and respiratory therapy in patients before oncological gastric or esophageal resection with regard to postoperative complications and mortality.

interventions.name: Implementation of a prehabilitation program consisting of sports and exercise therapy, nutritional therapy (high-calorie diet) and respiratory therapy for the duration of the initial consultation until surgery (varies between 3-4 weeks).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
planned oncological gastric or esophageal resection + receipt of neoadjuvant therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of legal capacity
Lack of patient consent
Presence of pregnancy
Primary surgery without neoadjuvant therapy
